newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates end easy on good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates end easy on good liquidity.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 2.50 percent, down from the opening 3.00-3.50 percent on improved liquidity, dealers said.

"The market was quite easy today," a dealer at state-run bank said. "Liquidity has been good the past couple of months and has improved on Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention in the foreign exchange market."

The RBI has been buying dollars in the foreign exchange market to prevent the rupee from appreciaitng. RBI dollar purchases have released rupees to the banking system and boosted liquidity, dealers said.
Prices of government securities fell in moderate trade, dealers said.
"The prices were too high," a dealer at foreign bank said. "We are now seeing a correction."
Tuesday's trades on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were worth 1.28 billion rupess against Monday's 750 million, an NSE dealer said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 government stock fell to 103.06 rupees from 103.13 and the 13.40 percent 1999 stock to 101.98 from 102.03, dealers said.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in May was unchanged at 8.10 percent while April bills yielded 7.42 percent against the last traded yield of 7.31 percent, they said.
